programme: PAX7 and HEYL form a Notch-pathway stem/progenitor quiescence circuit: PAX7 induces the Notch receptors NOTCH1 and NOTCH3 (alongside canonical myogenic differentiation genes PAX3, MYOG, CKM, ENO3 and the HES/HEY partners ID2/ID3), while HEYL — itself a canonical Notch target gene — in turn drives the core Notch effector genes HES1, HEY1 and HEY2, plus the androgen receptor AR. Together their target sets trace a self-reinforcing Notch signalling loop that gates whether a tissue-resident progenitor stays quiescent or exits into differentiation.
role_in_a: In multiple sclerosis, PAX7+ satellite cells are the resident muscle stem-cell pool; the retrieved record (PMID 27303309) documents a fibre-type-specific decline of this myogenic stem cell compartment in MS patients that high-intensity training can partially reverse — i.e. PAX7-marked progenitors and their regenerative output are measurably compromised in this disease.
role_in_b: In testicular cancer there is no retrieved evidence for either factor. Mechanistically, the same PAX7/Notch/HEY-effector circuit would be expected to operate in the testis, where PAX7 marks a discrete spermatogonial stem-cell subpopulation and Notch/HEY signalling together with androgen-receptor (AR) input govern germ-cell niche quiescence versus differentiation — a plausible substrate for tumours that arise from progenitors failing to exit self-renewal, but this is inference, not a documented finding here.
shared_axis: If both diseases reflect dysregulation of the same PAX7-anchored, Notch-effector-gated progenitor-quiescence circuit — in the satellite-cell niche of skeletal muscle for MS and the spermatogonial niche of the testis for testicular cancer — that would explain why the same two factors recur across cohorts of both diseases without either disease being a cause of the other.
reasoning: The Notch/HES-HEY module is genuinely present in the given target-gene sets (not an outside import), and PAX7 has one direct citation placing its progenitor pool in MS. But HEYL itself has zero literature or Open Targets support in either disease, testicular cancer has no evidence for any of the 12 factors at all, and the brain/muscle–testis pairing is not obvious from anatomy or clinical practice — so the programme is nameable but the case for these two diseases sharing it rests almost entirely on reasoning about target-gene identity, not retrieval.
support: PMID 27303309 — reports fibre-type-specific decline of PAX7+ myogenic satellite/stem cells in multiple sclerosis patients, partially reversible with high-intensity training; this is the only retrieved evidence for any carrying factor in either disease. No PMID in the material places HEYL, NOTCH1/NOTCH3, HES1/HEY1/HEY2, or AR in either disease, and none place any factor in Testicular_Cancer — 'none found' for that entire half of the account.
how_to_falsify: Profile PAX7+ progenitor populations in matched MS muscle biopsies and in testicular germ-cell-tumour tissue (single-cell RNA-seq or IHC) for co-expression of the HEYL/HES1/HEY1/HEY2/NOTCH1/NOTCH3 module; if PAX7+ cells in either tissue do not show coordinated Notch-effector activity, or if the module is altered in only one tissue and not the other, the shared-axis claim fails.
caveats: Brain/muscle (MS) and testis (cancer) are anatomically unrelated tissues, and the 286 patient-group comparisons come from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so high recurrence counts reflect correlated subgroups within few underlying cohorts rather than many independent replications. Testicular_Cancer carries zero Open Targets or literature signal for all 12 listed factors, so role_in_b is unverified inference. Ten of the twelve concordant factors (SALL1, POU4F1, HOXD8, ZBTB32, INSM1, ONECUT1, DEAF1, CDX2, ONECUT1, KLF4, PATZ1) sit outside the named Notch/PAX7 module and are not claimed to be part of this account — most have no retrieved literature for either disease and should not be read as corroborating it. The single-view exclusions (POU3F1, NRG1, ZNF398, MEIS3, HOXD1, KLF11, PRDM10, DMRTA1) and tissue-generic exclusions (including NRG1, ASCL1, SOX2, REST — general neural/stem-cell regulators) were removed before ranking, which is why no broader neural-stem-cell master regulator appears here; that absence is the filter working, not a gap in the account.
